_about: Knowledge-graph edges. Cross-commodity rules, chapter notes, classification ordering, exclusion rules. The retrieval layer surfaces relevant edges to the LLM at refinement time so question phrasing and tie-breaks are grounded in real interpretive rules.

edges.title: Chapter 64: outer sole material first
edges.body: In Chapter 64 (footwear), classification is driven first by the constituent material of the outer sole, then by the upper material. This is established by HSEN to Chapter 64 and is the standard GIR 1 approach for footwear.

edges.title: Plug-assembled vs other (6402)
edges.body: Within heading 6402 (footwear with outer soles and uppers of rubber or plastics), 6402.20 specifically covers footwear with upper straps or thongs assembled to the sole by means of plugs. This is the classic flip-flop. Other 6402 items (6402.91, 6402.99) are not plug-assembled.

edges.title: Ankle coverage in 6403 leather footwear
edges.body: Within 6403, sub-headings split on whether the footwear covers the ankle (e.g. boots) or not (e.g. shoes). 6403.5x covers footwear with leather soles; 6403.9x covers other soles. Boots covering the ankle attract different sub-headings to low-cut shoes.

edges.title: Sports footwear definition
edges.body: Sports footwear (6404.11) is defined to include shoes designed for a sporting activity which has, or has provision for, the attachment of spikes, sprigs, cleats, stops, clips, bars or the like; and skating boots, ski-boots, cross-country ski-footwear, wrestling boots, boxing boots and cycling shoes. General gym shoes, trainers and sneakers also qualify.

edges.title: Alcohol strength context for Chapter 22 beverages
edges.body: Beverages in Chapter 22 use alcohol strength, beverage type, and presentation as important classification context. Record ABV and product type when distinguishing wine, beer, spirits, and low-strength beverages.

edges.title: Alcohol strength bands for product distinction
edges.body: Alcoholic beverages can require ABV banding for product distinction: below 1.2%, 1.2-3.4%, 3.5-8.4%, 8.5-22%, and 22%+. Use these bands only as classification context in this app.

edges.title: Chapter 73: material first, then product type
edges.body: In Chapter 73 (other articles of iron or steel), classification depends first on the type of steel (stainless vs other iron/steel) and then on the product type (sink, kitchenware, cooking appliance, etc.). Cutlery is excluded and falls in Chapter 82.

edges.title: Cutlery is excluded from Chapter 73
edges.body: Knives, forks, spoons and other cutlery are excluded from heading 7323 (kitchenware) and fall in Chapter 82 (tools, cutlery). Do not classify a kitchen knife under 7323 even if it is stainless steel.
